chunks: They will hear no vain talk there, but only salutations of peace, and they will have their sustenance morning and evening.
ai.seo_question: What kind of speech do the inhabitants of Paradise hear, and when do they receive their sustenance?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the absence of 'laghw' (idle talk) signifies the purification of the tongue and heart from all vanity, leaving only 'salam' as the essence of divine greeting. The continuous provision ('rizq') in the morning and evening underscores the eternal freshness and lack of depletion in Paradise's blessings, reflecting the concept of 'baqa' (permanence) distinct from the transient nature of worldly sustenance.
